correctness.rationale: Each image of the entire direct product is the Cartesian product of the two coordinate images. In the first factor, equality of terminal states means that the counts of b-moves from n−1 have all n different residues; one trajectory therefore makes at least n−1 such moves. Between consecutive such moves it needs at least n−1 rotations, forcing the scattered subsequence R; swapping letters forces its mate. In an embedding of a common subsequence in R, each selected a-run uses a source a-run distinct from those used by the other selected a-runs, and each consecutive pair within a selected b-run skips a distinct source a-run disjoint from those. The swapped inequality gives the bound 2(n−2) on the shared subsequence length, attained by (ab)^(n−2). Shared positions in any two embeddings form a common subsequence, so their union gives the claimed lower bound independently of the reset construction. For n≥5, the first prefix leaves {0,1} and a second image missing 0 and n−2; after a² these are {2,3} and {0,…,n−3}. Each of the next n−5 blocks advances the first pair and reduces the second interval by one; the final blocks then produce {1},{0}. The total length is 3+n(n−3)+2+n(n−5)+(n−1)+2+n=2(n²−3n+3). The three small words act as claimed. Independent multi-target backward preimage BFS in /workspace/review_checks/5.py confirms lengths 2,6,14,26,42,62,86,114 for n=2,…,9 and replays the witnesses through n=32. Finite checks are corroboration, not proof for all n.

value.rationale: Two individually extremal factors share one input but disagree on the roles of both letters. The result determines an exact infinite-family synchronization cost: nearly additive, yet with a sharp saving of 2n−4 over separate resetting. The matched LCS obstruction and image-set witness explain why the saving is attainable, beyond numerical observation or the generic max-to-sum interval. No general product classification or shortest-word multiplicities are claimed.
